x: Under Article 342 the President, after consultation with the Governor, notifies the Scheduled Tribes of a State or UT (the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950). Parliament only includes or excludes communities later by law; the Governor and the Council of Ministers do not notify the list.

Municipalities (and Nagar Panchayats) in AP are governed by the AP Municipalities Act, 1965, and Municipal Corporations by the AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 (as CDCA cites it; some 2026 reports name a 1955 Corporations Act). Options A and B swap or misdate the two Acts, and D names a Panchayats Act.

As per the Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, AP's 123 urban local bodies are 17 Municipal Corporations, 76 Municipalities and 30 Nagar Panchayats. (The 2024-25 Survey counted 79 municipalities and 27 nagar panchayats, so year-specific counts differ.)

Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: 19 model Gram Panchayats covering 43 Gram Sabhas are being developed. Pairs 3 and 4 are wrong: AP's amending Act came in 1998 and the AP PESA Rules in 2011, so the years are interchanged.

Under PESA, any provision of a State Panchayat law inconsistent with it ceases to operate one year from the date PESA received assent (24 December 1996), unless amended earlier. Six months, two years and five years are not the stated period.

Article 243K provides the State Election Commission for Panchayat (local-body) elections. Article 243ZA extends the same SEC to municipal elections, not the Governor's appointment; Article 243A concerns the Gram Sabha; and Article 243C deals with the composition of Panchayats, not municipal rolls.

After bifurcation, the Governor constituted the State Election Commission for the residuary State of AP on 30 January 2016 (APPSC-GS 2022 key). 2 June 2014 is the bifurcation date, 1 November 2014 is not linked to the SEC, and 24 April 1994 is close to the AP Panchayat Raj Act (21 April 1994) and the 73rd Amendment's anniversary, not the SEC.
As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, social protection covers about 64.3% of India's population, up from 22% in 2016. The 22% figure is the 2016 level, not the current one.
